headline: CORRECTION -- 0300 triage hold on '350,000 without power in Dnipro' LIFTED
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- reconciled] Reuters (via DZRH/Daily Sabah) reports governor Hanzha saying a day of attacks cut power to 350,000 households in Dnipro; Kyiv Post independently reports Hanzha's Telegram: 'more than 350,000 customers in the city and nearby settlements have been left without…
sources: Dnipropetrovsk governor Oleksandr Hanzha via Telegram, carried by Reuters; DTEK + Ukrenergo via AFP/Malay Mail
fault_line: 350,000 cut, 200,000 still dark a day later: is Dnipro's grid being degraded faster than crews can repair it before winter?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- reconciled] Reuters (via DZRH/Daily Sabah) reports governor Hanzha saying a day of attacks cut power to 350,000 households in Dnipro; Kyiv Post independently reports Hanzha's Telegram: 'more than 350,000 customers in the city and nearby settlements have been left without electricity' after overnight strikes Oct 29-30. [VERIFIED FACT -- remainder] AFP/Malay Mail Oct 30: more than 200,000 people remained without power in Dnipropetrovsk region, while DTEK said Ukrenergo ordered emergency cuts and the governor said power was restored to 'most consumers'. CORRECTION TO 0300-06: the 350k figure is NOT uncorroborated repackaging -- it is the governor's peak figure carried by Reuters; the apparent conflict with 200k+ is peak (Oct 29) vs remainder (Oct 30). The 0300 hold is lifted for the peak figure with this dating attached. Dnipro station death toll stands at 14 (Reuters) to 15 (CNN/NV, incl. the overnight repeat strike) -- toll discrepancy by time of count, not a new strike in-window.
sections.what_verified: Reuters T1 + AFP T1 for the two numbers at their two moments; Kyiv Post (unregistered) agrees on the 350k governor quote.
sections.what_disputed: None on the numbers once dated; CNN's 15 vs Reuters' 14 station toll reflects the overnight repeat strike count, not a contradiction.
sections.why_matters: Correction with a number that matters: 350,000 was Dnipro's peak blackout, confirmed by Reuters -- and a day later 200,000 were still without power. The grid is losing the repair race.
sections.context: Background: CORRECTION -- 0300 triage hold on '350,000 without power in Dnipro' LIFTED: Reuters confirms governor's 350,000 figure as the Oct 29 peak; AFP/DTEK 200,000+ is the Oct 30 remainder -- both true, different moments

totw_analysis: Our read: Correction with a number that matters: 350,000 was Dnipro's peak blackout, confirmed by Reuters -- and a day later 200,000 were still without power. The grid is losing the repair race. The fault line our audience is arguing over: 350,000 cut, 200,000 still dark a day later: is Dnipro's grid being degraded faster than crews can repair it before winter?
